core_obligations: Setup (proof lines 966-975): for a fixed family of sheaves the author collects the set of maps that would have to be killed and bounds its cardinality, so that only that set of data matters.

The bound (proof lines 976-988): choosing an ordinal of cofinality larger than that cardinal, the author shows that each map into a later stage factors through an earlier one, by counting the possible positions of the finitely many pieces of data involved.
Conclusion (proof lines 989-994): the lifting statement for sets and the existence of ordinals of large cofinality give the asserted factorisation, which is the statement.
proof_roadmap: Bound the set of maps that need to be killed.
Choose an ordinal of larger cofinality and count the positions of the data.
Use the lifting statement for sets to get the factorisation.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a fixed set of abelian sheaves there is an ordinal such that every map from one of them into a stage of the transfinite construction factors through an earlier stage (statement lines 956-964). The proof is a complete argument: the set of maps that have to be killed is collected and bounded (proof lines 966-975); an ordinal of cofinality larger than that bound is chosen, and the positions of the finitely many pieces of data are counted to show the factorisation (proof lines 976-988); and the lifting statement for sets together with the existence of ordinals of large cofinality gives the result (proof lines 989-994). The non-formal content is the counting argument. The claim is H2.
